author: Ocean World project, authored with Codex
geometry: Original Hermite body cross-sections with continuous shoulders and broad humpback head, dolphin melon/beak, original closed fins and flukes. No third-party mesh or texture copied; triangle count retained.
redistribution: This new project-authored content has no additional third-party asset restrictions. It can accompany redistribution of the project. The scientific reference pages are cited only; their photos and illustrations are not bundled.

legacyStage06.note: The archived stage-06 tag remains unchanged; this is a new appearance/motion version.

models.name: 座头鲸
models.measurement: Head-to-tail total length; longitudinal geometry spans exactly 1.0 before metre scaling.
models.authenticity: Authored visual representative; not a scan, measured individual, calibrated anatomy or natural population simulation.
models.largeShapeReferences: Mostly dark dorsal body, pale variable underside, long pectoral fins, small posterior dorsal hump, broad horizontal flukes, head tubercles and paired blowholes.
models.choreography: Continuous forward-tangent posture, controlled ascent, partial swell following, actual exposed-blowhole breath gate, controlled descent and stroke/glide bouts.

models.name: 宽吻海豚
models.measurement: Head-to-tail total length; longitudinal geometry spans exactly 1.0 before metre scaling.
models.authenticity: Authored visual representative; not a scan, measured individual, calibrated anatomy or natural population simulation.
models.largeShapeReferences: Gray dorsal body, pale underside, continuous short blunt beak with forehead, swept dorsal fin, paired pectoral fins, horizontal flukes and one blowhole.
models.choreography: Six finite fixed-step followers, bounded neighbour separation, individual steering and one 40–60s formation change; no persistent ecology.

motionReferences.author: Frank E. Fish
motionReferences.usage: Posterior bending and fluke heave/pitch; active dolphin peak-to-peak tail displacement of approximately .20 body lengths. Frequency fit f=.47+.37U used only inside observed 1.22–6.0m/s range; slower states fade toward glide rather than extrapolate.

motionReferences.author: Goldbogen et al.
motionReferences.usage: Body orientation, velocity, strokes/glides and respiratory exposure must relate; study-specific California foraging speeds and diving depths are not asserted for this Caribbean display.

limits: Reference-informed authored display, not a calibrated fluid, respiration or autonomous population simulation.
Wave exposure is evaluated at the actual whale nose and shared global water time.
Followers are a finite deterministic controller with one authored formation change; social intent and biological motivation are not inferred.
Whale beat amplitude/frequency and breath timing remain display choices; no measured individual is claimed.
No new photos, source meshes, downloaded animation or third-party asset licence.
Technical checks cannot establish visual acceptance.
concentratedCorrection: Whale smoothly turns into the far water after its surface breath; the 65–80s retrospective camera pulls back to retain both independent observation subjects.
